$comment: Real-time (GTFS-RT) service settings; see docs/skytrain-viz-PLAN.md §4.6. Upstream request rate is fixed by the poll schedule no matter how many clients connect.
$poll: TransLink's Open API terms allow an API key 'a maximum of 1,000 requests per day' (https://www.translink.ca/about-us/doing-business-with-translink/app-developer-resources/terms-of-use, checked 2026-09-29; unclear whether that covers GTFS-RT). Until TransLink says otherwise, the leader stays under dailyCap across all three feeds in any 24 hours (a ledger in var/rt-history/requests.json enforces it across restarts), polling most often at peak. Bands (local time) are guesses at when buses are busiest; at most ~970 in any 24 hours (~965 on a weekday, ~815 on a weekend day) (packages/transit-core/src/rt/budget.ts, test/rt-budget.test.ts). Holidays run the weekday schedule. SkyTrain alerts with a recognised operating change become draft disruptions (docs/skytrain-viz-PLAN.md §4.10), so alertsS delays drafts by up to that long. OPEN-QUESTIONS #29.
$staleGraceS: Clients treat live data as unavailable (and fall back to schedule estimates) once it's this much older than the positions poll interval. Was 120 s at a fixed 20 s interval.
$coverageSlackS: Recorder coverage breaks when consecutive snapshots are further apart than the positions poll interval plus this. Was 75 s at a fixed 20 s interval.
$interpolateSlackS: Interpolate a vehicle between two observations only when they are at most the positions poll interval plus this apart. Was 180 s at a fixed 20 s interval.
$extrapolateSlackS: At the live edge, predict a vehicle forward along its route for at most the positions poll interval plus this (fixes are already ~20-60 s old when fetched). Was 90 s at a fixed 20 s interval.
$detourNearM: A bus off its route while a TransLink detour alert covers it counts as on detour only within this distance of a stop the alert lists (guess; long-running detours would otherwise switch off shifted-GPS handling route-wide). See docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #28.
$dispatchCheckS: Live dispatch (docs/skytrain-viz-PLAN.md §4.11): how often the RT service checks regions/metro-vancouver/observations and regions/metro-vancouver/disruptions for changes. Only changed inputs re-dispatch a date; client requests never do.
$dispatchWindowDays: Live dispatch covers service dates this many days either side of today; older and later dates come from build:dispatch.
$prediction: Live bus prediction and learned travel-time profiles (packages/transit-core/src/rt/profile.ts, docs/skytrain-viz-PLAN.md §4.5). Values are guesses tuned against recorded data with pipelines/eval-rt.ts unless noted; see docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #25.

prediction.$bandStartHours: Time-of-day bands: night, AM peak, midday, PM peak, evening (local hours).
prediction.$stationaryM: GPS noise on a standing bus is ~5-10 m (measured: recorded fixes).
prediction.$stopExcessM: Slow time within this of a stop (vs the median pace of bins away from stops within baselineWindowM) is counted as dwell, since 30 s fixes smear dwells into nearby bins. Tuned with pipelines/eval-rt.ts (2026-09-26): 75 m gives dwells of p25/p50/p75 22/32/45 s (plausible for RapidBus stops at signals) for ~2 m median / ~12 m p90 more error at 60 s than 0 m (no concentration, where buses visibly don't stop); 150 m costs 5/30 m.
prediction.$paceWeight: Tuned on 8 h training / 3 h test (2026-09-26): adapting to the bus's recent pace (any window 180-1200 s) made 30-90 s predictions slightly worse, so it's off; re-test with more history.
prediction.$catchUpMps: Glide: tuned with pipelines/eval-rt.ts (2026-09-26): 8 m/s over ≤ 25 s keeps apparent speed p99 ≈ 24 m/s for ~1 m of median accuracy vs 12 m/s / 15 s.
prediction.$scheduleAnchorS: Schedule estimates for buses: TransLink gives every stop a time, interpolated between timepoints; pin to the timetable at most every this many seconds and let the profile place stops and slow sections in between. Guess.

$carry: Carrying RT bus delays into schedule estimates (packages/transit-core/src/rt/carry.ts). Guesses; see docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md #25.
